page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.48xlarge is a dedicated high-performance computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 96-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor operating at 3.7 GHz across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading disabled, allocating one vCPU per physical core. The system provides 768 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 5 GHz, delivering 8 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no local storage and does not feature a dedicated GPU, routing storage traffic and node communication over its 300 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate significant multi-core throughput and memory subsystem capacity. In stress-ng multi-core testing and PassMark CPU suites, the server scores 294,474.04 and 117,764.87 respectively, ranking in the top tier. The DDR5 memory delivers uncached read bandwidth of 701.06 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 353.58 GB/sec. Architectural support includes AVX-512 extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, facilitating accelerated matrix and vector operations for demanding mathematical tasks.

From an architectural perspective, the 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation avoids hyperthreading resource contention, ensuring consistent execution speed for tightly coupled parallel tasks. The absence of onboard NVMe storage necessitates network-attached storage architectures, balanced by the high-throughput 300 Gbps network fabric. This instance profile is engineered for computational fluid dynamics, weather forecasting, molecular dynamics simulations, and distributed engineering analysis.

It provides 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading disabled, paired with 768 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding 8 GB per core. The server contains no local storage and does not bundle hardware GPUs, relying on a 300 Gbps baseline network interface for cluster communication. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-core execution in stress-ng and PassMark, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth exceeding 701 GB/sec and native AVX-512 vector support. The hardware design prioritizes sustained compute and memory density without hyperthreading overhead, though disk I/O requires network storage. The hpc7a.48xlarge is engineered for computational fluid dynamics, scientific simulations, weather forecasting, and distributed high-performance computing workloads.
